Moroccan textiles are renowned for their vibrant colors, intricate patterns, and exceptional craftsmanship. Hand-embroidered fabrics, scarves, and shawls showcase delicate needlework that often tells stories or incorporates traditional motifs. Popular clothing items include the flowing kaftans and djellabas traditional robes worn by both men and women that are made from natural fibers such as wool, cotton, or silk. These garments often feature elaborate embroidery along the hems, sleeves, and collars, reflecting regional styles and cultural heritage. The rich hues ranging from deep reds and blues to earthy tones capture the essence of Morocco’s diverse landscapes and history. Whether worn for special occasions or everyday comfort, these textiles offer a beautiful blend of functionality and artistry. Collecting these pieces is a wonderful way to bring Moroccan culture into your wardrobe or home.
8. Argan Oil and Beauty Products

Argan oil, known as “liquid gold,” is a natural oil extracted from argan tree nuts, native to Morocco. It’s prized for its moisturizing and healing properties. You’ll find pure argan oil as well as soaps, creams, and hair products made from it. Make sure to buy from reputable sellers to ensure authenticity.

When shopping for these items, it’s good to take your time, ask questions about their origin, and observe the quality of the craftsmanship. These authentic products not only make fantastic souvenirs but also support Moroccan artisans and their centuries-old traditions.
How to Bargain in Moroccan Souks

Bargaining is an essential part of the shopping experience in Moroccan souks. It’s not just about getting a better price; it’s a social ritual that builds rapport and makes shopping fun and interactive. Here’s how to bargain like a local:
1. Start with a Friendly Greeting
Begin every interaction with a polite “Salam Alaikum” (peace be upon you) or “Bonjour” if you prefer French. A smile and friendly attitude go a long way in creating goodwill.
2. Ask for the Price
When you see something you like, ask for the price first. Sellers often quote a high initial price, expecting you to negotiate.
3. Offer a Lower Price
It’s common to start by offering about
half or even less than the asking price. This might feel bold, but it’s the norm in Moroccan markets. The seller will usually respond with a counteroffer.
4. Stay Polite and Patient
Keep the tone lighthearted and friendly. Bargaining is a dance be prepared for some back-and-forth. If you seem impatient or rude, the seller might refuse to negotiate.
5. Use Body Language
If you’re unsure about your language skills, non-verbal cues help. Shrugging, smiling, or pretending to walk away can signal your willingness to leave if the price isn’t right.
6. Know When to Walk Away
If the price doesn’t meet your budget or feels unfair, politely thank the seller, and start to leave. Often, this prompts the seller to offer a better price.
7. Learn a Few Key Phrases
Using local words shows respect and can improve your bargaining
“Bzaf” (too much)
“Qalil” (a little)
“Mashi mzyan” (not good)
“Smah li” (excuse me/sorry)
8. Don’t Take It Personally

Remember, bargaining is a game both sides enjoy. Sellers expect it, and no one is offended by a good negotiation. It’s part of the cultural experience and can even be a chance to connect and share a laugh.
Mastering the art of bargaining not only helps you get better deals but also makes your visit to the souks more engaging and memorable.
Avoiding Scams and Tourist Traps

While Moroccan souks offer an authentic and vibrant shopping experience, it’s important to stay alert to avoid common pitfalls and scams that sometimes target tourists. Here are some tips to help you shop safely and confidently:
1. Be Wary of Overly Pushy Sellers

Some vendors may pressure you aggressively to buy or follow you around the souk. Politely but firmly say no if you’re not interested and keep walking. It’s perfectly acceptable to ignore persistent sellers.
2. Watch for Fake or Low-Quality Products

If a deal sounds too good to be true, it probably is. Be cautious of items that look cheaply made or too perfect. For example, very cheap argan oil or rugs with uneven stitching might be low quality or counterfeit.
3. Know Basic Prices
Before you shop, research typical prices for key items like spices, rugs, or leather goods. This knowledge helps you spot unreasonable offers and avoid overpaying.
4. Beware of “Guides” or Helpers
Some people may approach you offering unsolicited help or guided tours inside the souk, then expect payment. Politely decline unless you want their service and have agreed on a price upfront.
5. Secure Your Belongings
Souks can get crowded and chaotic, which makes pickpocketing a risk. Keep your valuables close, use a money belt or a secure bag, and avoid flashing large amounts of cash or expensive items.
6. Use Cash Wisely
Most vendors prefer cash (Moroccan dirhams). Avoid exchanging money on the street and use official exchange bureaus or banks to get fair rates. Keep small bills handy for easier bargaining.
By staying aware and respectful, you’ll have a much more enjoyable and safe souk experience while supporting local artisans and businesses.
Additional Tips for a Great Souk Experience
To make the most of your visit to Moroccan souks, keep these practical tips in mind:
1. Best Times to Visit

Souks tend to be busiest mid-morning and late afternoon. For a more relaxed experience, visit early in the morning when the market is just waking up or later in the evening when it’s less crowded and cooler.
2. Dress Respectfully and Comfortably

Wear comfortable shoes for walking on uneven cobblestone streets. Dress modestly to respect local customs, especially in more traditional areas. Light, breathable fabrics are ideal for the warm Moroccan climate.
3. Carry Small Change
Have plenty of small bills and coins ready to make bargaining and small purchases easier. Vendors may not have change for large bills.
4. Plan How to Transport Your Purchases

If you buy large or fragile items, consider how you’ll carry them. Many shops will help package your goods securely. For big purchases, ask about shipping options or check if your hotel offers storage.
5. Stay Hydrated and Take Breaks
Walking through souks can be tiring. Drink plenty of water and take breaks in nearby cafés or tea houses to rest and soak in the local atmosphere.
6. Engage with Vendors Respectfully
Moroccan sellers are often eager to share the story behind their products. Showing genuine interest and respect can lead to better deals and a richer cultural experience.
Following these tips will help ensure your souk visit is enjoyable, comfortable, and rewarding.
Conclusion

Exploring Moroccan souks is an unforgettable journey into the heart of Morocco’s culture, craftsmanship, and everyday life. From vibrant rugs and exquisite leather goods to fragrant spices and dazzling jewelry, the souks offer a treasure trove of unique and authentic products. Learning to bargain respectfully not only helps you get the best prices but also connects you with the rich traditions and warm hospitality of Moroccan sellers.

With a little preparation and an open mind, your souk adventure will be more than just shopping it will be an immersive cultural experience filled with sights, sounds, and stories that stay with you long after you leave. So get ready to dive into the vibrant maze of Morocco’s markets and discover the perfect souvenirs to bring home.

title: The Complete Travel Guide to Ouarzazate: Gateway to the Sahara
seoTitle: Travel Guide to Ouarzazate: Gateway to the Sahara
description: Planning a trip to Ouarzazate? Discover top attractions, film studios, desert tours, kasbahs, and local tips in this complete guide to Morocco’s desert.

blocks.x: Introduction: Why Visit Ouarzazate?

Tucked between the rugged High Atlas Mountains and the vast sands of the Sahara, Ouarzazate is a city like no other in Morocco. Often called “The Door of the Desert,” it’s a place where ancient kasbahs, sweeping landscapes, and cinematic magic come together to create an unforgettable destination. While many travelers pass through on their way to the Sahara, those who linger discover a city rich in culture, history, and adventure.

Ouarzazate has long been a favorite for filmmakers, serving as the backdrop for iconic films and series like Gladiator , Game of Thrones , and Lawrence of Arabia . Beyond the silver screen, visitors are drawn by the earthy tones of its desert architecture, the hospitality of its Berber communities, and the serenity of its oases. Whether you're exploring ancient fortresses, riding camels through golden dunes, or touring legendary film studios, Ouarzazate delivers an immersive Moroccan experience that blends tradition with cinematic flair.

In this guide, we’ll walk you through everything you need to know for your visit how to get there, what to see, where to stay, and how to make the most of your time in one of Morocco’s most fascinating cities.
How to Get to Ouarzazate

Despite its remote location, Ouarzazate is accessible by multiple modes of transport , making it easier than you might think to reach this desert gem. Whether you’re flying in directly or combining your trip with visits to Marrakech or the Sahara, here’s how to plan your journey.
By Air

Ouarzazate Airport (OZZ) receives domestic flights from major Moroccan cities like Casablanca and Marrakech , as well as occasional international flights from cities in Europe. Royal Air Maroc and other regional carriers operate regular routes, making air travel one of the quickest ways to reach the city.
By Road from Marrakech

The most popular route is a drive from Marrakech , which takes around 4 to 5 hours via the dramatic Tizi n’Tichka Pass . This journey through the High Atlas Mountains offers breathtaking views and the chance to stop at scenic villages and sites like Aït Ben Haddou .
By Bus or Shared Taxi

Several companies, including CTM and Supratours , offer comfortable and affordable bus rides from cities like Marrakech, Fes, or Agadir. Shared grand taxis are another option for those looking for a more local experience, although comfort and timing may vary.
Best Time to Visit Ouarzazate

Ouarzazate, sitting at the gateway to the Sahara Desert, has a semi-arid climate hot summers, cool winters, and lots of sunshine year-round. Choosing when to visit depends on what you’re hoping to experience.
Spring (March to May)

Spring is arguably the best time to visit. The weather is mild and pleasant, making it ideal for exploring kasbahs, hiking in nearby valleys, and even heading out on desert adventures. Wildflowers bloom across the landscapes, and the Atlas Mountains are still capped with snow, offering stunning backdrops.
Autumn (September to November)
Another great season to visit, autumn offers warm days and cool evenings without the scorching summer heat. It’s also a popular time for cultural events and less crowded sightseeing.
Summer (June to August)

Summer can be extremely hot, with temperatures soaring above 40°C (104°F), especially in July and August. However, if you're well-prepared and plan indoor or shaded activities during peak heat hours, it can still be a rewarding trip—especially for budget travelers, as prices tend to drop.
Winter (December to February)

Winters in Ouarzazate are cool but sunny. Daytime temperatures remain comfortable, though nights can get quite chilly. It’s a good time for quiet travel and photography, with fewer tourists and clear skies over kasbahs and deserts.
Top Attractions in Ouarzazate

Ouarzazate may be small, but it’s packed with historical landmarks, cinematic treasures, and awe-inspiring natural landscapes. Whether you’re a history buff, a movie lover, or an adventurer, the city and its surroundings offer something truly special.
Atlas Studios – The Hollywood of the Desert

Dubbed the “Hollywood of Africa,” Atlas Studios is the largest film studio in the world by land area. Countless international blockbusters and TV shows have been filmed here, including Gladiator , Game of Thrones , The Mummy , and Kingdom of Heaven . Visitors can take guided tours through elaborate sets, ancient city replicas, and desert landscapes used in these iconic productions. It’s a must-visit for cinema enthusiasts and a unique insight into Morocco’s thriving film industry.
Kasbah Taourirt – A Glimpse into Royal Berber Life

Located in the heart of Ouarzazate, this magnificent 19th-century kasbah was once the residence of the powerful Glaoui family. With its labyrinth of mud-brick rooms, intricate Berber decorations, and panoramic views from the upper floors, Kasbah Taourirt offers a fascinating peek into the architectural and cultural heritage of southern Morocco. A guided tour helps you uncover the stories hidden within its fortified walls.
Aït Ben Haddou – A UNESCO World Heritage Site

Just 30 km from Ouarzazate lies Aït Ben Haddou , an ancient, fortified village (ksar) that’s arguably one of Morocco’s most iconic landmarks. Built with traditional clay architecture, this UNESCO World Heritage Site has been used as a backdrop in countless films. Walking through its narrow alleys feels like stepping back in time, and the views from the hilltop granary are nothing short of spectacular.
Fint Oasis – A Hidden Desert Paradise

A short drive from Ouarzazate reveals Fint Oasis , a lush, serene haven tucked between rugged desert hills. With its palm groves, traditional mud villages, and flowing river, it offers a tranquil escape from the city. You can enjoy a peaceful walk along the water, meet local families, or simply relax with a mint tea while soaking in the oasis views. It’s a perfect half-day trip that showcases the surprising greenery of the desert.
The Cinema Museum

Opposite Kasbah Taourirt, this unique museum is housed in a former studio and showcases props, costumes, and old film equipment from movies shot in the region. It’s a compact but fascinating stop that celebrates the city’s connection to the global film industry. Don’t miss the chance to explore old sets and learn how Ouarzazate became a world-famous filming destination.
Where to Stay in Ouarzazate

Ouarzazate offers a range of accommodation options for every kind of traveler, whether you're looking for luxury, comfort, or an authentic Moroccan experience. From stylish riads to desert lodges, here are the best areas and types of stays to consider:
Luxury Hotels and Resorts

For travelers seeking comfort and elegance, Ouarzazate is home to a few well-appointed luxury hotels. Many offers stunning desert views, swimming pools to cool off in the midday heat, and traditional Moroccan architecture with modern amenities. Popular options include Le Berbère Palace , a five-star property with lush gardens and cinematic décor, and Dar Chamaa , a boutique hotel that blends charm and tranquility.
Traditional Riads and Guesthouses

If you’re after a more authentic and intimate experience, staying in a riad or guesthouse is the way to go. These family-run accommodations often feature traditional design, homemade meals, and personalized hospitality. Properties like Riad Bouchedor and Riad Ouarzazate offer beautifully decorated rooms and a chance to engage with local culture in a relaxed setting.
Desert Lodges and Eco-Stays

For something unique, head just outside the city to stay in eco-lodges or desert camps . These accommodations let you wake up to panoramic desert views and stargaze at night under clear skies. Many also offer camel rides, guided hikes, or cooking classes. Staying at places like Ecolodge La Palmeraie or Camp Boujou adds an adventurous twist to your trip while supporting sustainable tourism.
Budget-Friendly Options

Backpackers and budget-conscious travelers will also find plenty of affordable hotels and hostels. Basic yet comfortable, these spots offer great value, and many include free breakfast or guided excursion options. Hostels such as Hotel Nadia or Maison d’Hôte La Roche Noire are popular among solo travelers and groups alike.
Whether you prefer a luxurious resort, a cozy riad, or a night under the stars, Ouarzazate has accommodation choices to suit all travel styles and budgets.
What to Eat in Ouarzazate

Ouarzazate offers a delicious introduction to the hearty, spice-rich flavors of southern Moroccan cuisine. Whether you’re dining in a family-run eatery or enjoying a meal at a luxury riad, the food here reflects the region’s Amazigh (Berber), Arab, and Saharan influences. Here are the must-try dishes and culinary experiences you shouldn't miss:
Tagine Varieties

Tagine is a staple of Moroccan cuisine, and in Ouarzazate, you’ll find regional twists on this classic slow-cooked dish. Try lamb with prunes and almonds , chicken with preserved lemons and olives , or vegetable tagine seasoned with saffron and cumin. The best part? Many restaurants use locally grown ingredients for fresher, more vibrant flavors.
Mechoui and Grilled Meats

In many local eateries, you’ll encounter mechoui —a whole lamb roasted in a clay oven until it’s tender and juicy. Grilled meats are also popular here, often served with fresh bread, herbed couscous, and spicy harissa. Ask for brochettes (skewers), a go-to street food that’s quick, flavorful, and satisfying.
Amazigh-Inspired Dishes

Southern Morocco has a strong Amazigh heritage, and this is reflected in its cuisine. Try Amlou , a rich dip made from almonds, argan oil, and honey, or Berber pizza (medfouna), a stuffed flatbread cooked over hot stones. These dishes are often homemade and give insight into centuries-old food traditions.
Traditional Sweets and Mint Tea

End your meal with Moroccan pastries like chebakia (sesame cookies in honey) or briouats (sweet almond-filled pastries). Pair them with freshly brewed mint tea , often poured from a height to create froth—an art as much as a ritual. The tea is more than a drink; it’s a gesture of hospitality you’ll experience everywhere.
Where to Eat

Some of the best dining experiences in Ouarzazate come from modest family-run restaurants and open-air cafés. For a mix of ambiance and authentic food, visit Kasbah Tafarnout , Douyria , or Le Jardin des Aromes . For a quick bite or snack, street vendors around the medina offer fresh msemen (Moroccan pancakes), olives, and dates.
Ouarzazate’s food scene is simple, soulful, and deeply rooted in local culture perfect for food lovers who want to taste the real Morocco.
Best Day Trips and Excursions from Ouarzazate

Ouarzazate is more than just a scenic city it’s a strategic launching pad for some of Morocco’s most unforgettable landscapes and historical gems. Whether you're an adventure seeker, culture enthusiast, or nature lover, the area around Ouarzazate offers a wide array of experiences just a short drive away. Here’s a deeper look at the top day trips and excursions you shouldn't miss:
Dades and Todgha Gorges – Nature’s Sculpted Masterpieces

Stretching across the eastern High Atlas, these two gorges are natural wonders carved by the forces of wind and water over millennia. Dades Gorge is known for its dramatic red-rock formations, winding roads like the “Monkey Fingers,” and panoramic viewpoints perfect for photography. Meanwhile, Todgha Gorge offers towering limestone cliffs that rise up to 300 meters, attracting climbers from around the world.

Stop along the way at traditional Berber villages where locals sell crafts and carpets and enjoy mint tea with a view. These gorges are ideal for scenic drives, easy hikes, or more challenging treks for outdoor enthusiasts.
Zagora – Gateway to the Sahara

For travelers eager to taste the magic of the desert without heading deep into the Erg Chebbi dunes, Zagora offers an excellent compromise. Often referred to as “the door to the Sahara,” this desert town provides everything from camel rides through rolling dunes to nights under the stars in traditional Berber tents.

While the dunes here are smaller than those in Merzouga, the surrounding palm groves, kasbahs, and dramatic desert plateaus offer a surreal and serene experience. It's perfect for a quick desert getaway or an overnight excursion filled with music, storytelling, and authentic Moroccan cuisine.
Kasbah Telouet – Off the Beaten Path

Less visited but equally fascinating, Kasbah Telouet was once the palace of the powerful Glaoui family, rulers of southern Morocco during the French protectorate. Though some sections are crumbling, others have been beautifully restored, showcasing stunning zellige tilework, carved cedar wood ceilings, and traditional mosaics.

Set high in the Atlas Mountains along the former caravan route, Telouet offers visitors a glimpse into Morocco’s feudal past without the crowds of more famous sites. The journey itself winding through mountain roads with panoramic views is an adventure.
Cultural Tips for Visitors to Ouarzazate

While Ouarzazate is a welcoming and relatively relaxed destination, understanding local customs and etiquette will help you connect more deeply with the culture and people. Here are some useful tips to ensure a respectful and rewarding experience:
Respect Local Customs

Morocco is a predominantly Muslim country, and while Ouarzazate is used to tourists, modesty is still appreciated. Dress conservatively, especially when visiting religious sites or rural villages covering shoulders and knees is a good rule of thumb. During Ramadan, be mindful of locals fasting during daylight hours and avoid eating or drinking in public at that time.
Learn a Few Phrases

While French and Arabic are widely spoken, many locals also speak Amazigh (Berber). Learning a few basic greetings like “Salam alaikum” (peace be upon you) or “Shukran” (thank you) will be greatly appreciated and can help build genuine rapport with residents and vendors.
Haggling is Normal

Bargaining is part of daily life in Morocco, especially in souks and markets. Don’t be shy vendors expect negotiation. Just remember to stay polite and smile while you bargain. It’s as much about social interaction as it is about the sale.
Ask Before Taking Photos
Always ask permission before photographing people, particularly women and children. Many locals are happy to pose if asked respectfully but taking photos without consent can be seen as intrusive.
Support Local Artisans

Ouarzazate and its surroundings are known for beautiful handwoven carpets, pottery, silver jewelry, and leather goods. When you buy directly from artisans or women’s cooperatives, you not only get a unique souvenir but also support the local economy in a meaningful way.
Shopping in Ouarzazate: What to Buy and Where to Go

While Ouarzazate is best known for its cinematic history and stunning kasbahs, it also offers a rewarding shopping experience that reflects the craftsmanship and cultural diversity of southern Morocco.
Handicrafts & Berber Art

One of the best things to shop for in Ouarzazate is traditional Berber handicrafts. You'll find intricate woven rugs , handmade jewelry , and colorful pottery often crafted by Amazigh artisans from nearby villages. These items aren’t just souvenirs; they’re cultural treasures that carry centuries of tradition.
Textiles & Tuareg Accessories

Markets and artisan shops are rich with Tuareg-style silver jewelry , leather goods , and vibrant textiles . Scarves dyed with natural pigments, embroidered fabrics, and camel-hair blankets are not only beautiful but also practical, especially for desert travelers.
Where to Shop
Ensemble Artisanal: A government-run cooperative showcasing quality artisan goods at fair prices. Great for rugs, lamps, and ceramics without the need to haggle.
Local Souks (Markets): Smaller, traditional souks operate throughout the week. They’re perfect for practicing your bargaining skills and discovering unique, locally made items.
Shops near Taourirt Kasbah: These offer a mix of antiques, textiles, and handcrafted décor items often with sellers willing to share the stories behind the goods.
Final Thoughts

Ouarzazate is far more than just a stop on the way to the Sahara it’s a destination, offering a unique blend of cinematic history, ancient kasbahs, dramatic landscapes, and deep-rooted Berber culture. Whether you're exploring iconic film sets, journeying through desert landscapes, shopping for artisan crafts, or simply soaking in the peaceful atmosphere, Ouarzazate delivers a truly immersive Moroccan experience.

Its quieter pace compared to larger cities makes it perfect for travelers seeking authenticity, adventure, and a deeper connection to Morocco’s southern soul. Add it to your itinerary, and you’ll leave with unforgettable memories and probably a few beautiful handmade souvenirs too.

title: THE EXCITEMENTS THAT YOU CAN FIND IN FEZ.
seoTitle: THE EXCITEMENTS THAT YOU CAN FIND IN FEZ.
description: When we're talking about the Moroccan Kingdom, especially when we're talking about it's inception, we are talking about Fez. This city was the capitol of M

blocks.x: by webdono
| fes city

When we're talking about the Moroccan Kingdom, especially when we're talking about it's inception, we are talking about Fez. This city was the capitol of Morocco, in which the first king settled, this happened 12 centuries ago. That's how old Fez is. Which means that it still preserves old buildings, and architectures from different periods of ancient history. The type of architectures we're talking about is of course, old islamic architecture and design.

Fez isn't however, all old and traditional, even though the ancient aspects of the city are what makes Fez a special city. In fact, Fez is the second largest city in Morocco. Which means it's a city with modern a lifestyle, since it's one of the imperial cities.
The modern face of Fez embraces all what has to do with the standards of modernity, like those you can find in European cities. From fancy restaurants and hotels to beautiful streets and so on.

Plus, Fez is in a geographical location that makes all the other places in Morocco that are considered the main attractions easily reachable. Fez is situated in the heart of Morocco. It's no wonder why it was the capitol of the first king.
You might be someone who is considering to pay a visit to Morocco, and fez in particular, and you might be wondering what sort of things you expect to do or find in there.
This article is about the most attractive things about Fez and the things you can do in there. Keep on reading to discover that.
The Medina .

Visiting Fez without taking a walk in the labyrinths of the old town, and even perhaps struggling to find your way around, is considered a waste of time. The old Medina is the original Fez, everything else is just added afterwards.
The old Medina is always crowded with people of all sorts, merchants selling goods, and bazaars all over the place in every corner of the narrow alleys.
The old Medina also has walls and castles from ancient history, these architectures are what give to Fez its authenticity.
These monuments are accumulated from as far as the 8th century of even before that. Those ancient architectures and buildings are what preserves the rich cultural heritage that Fez has.
One important thing is all the ancient mosques and their beautiful minarets are really hard to miss.
University of al-Qarawiyyin .

Fez is the home of the oldest university in the entire world. Although this might be a little bit surprising, but in fact, Morocco has this honour of hosting the first roots of academia. The one who established this university is woman whose name is Fatima Al-Fihri, she did so 1160 years ago. The whole world should be very thankful for what this lady has done, and perhaps recognize what she did more. In Morocco nowadays Fez is considered the capitol of science and knowledge, this reputation that Fez has comes from the University of al-Qarawiyyin.
This place is must-visit if you're considering Morocco for vacation.
Moroccan Riads.

A riad is essentially a form of Moroccan traditional style of housing, although the original form is said to be inspired from an old Roman city near Fez, called Volubilis. The old Moroccan dynasties adopted these types of houses, and soon they became the norm for many Moroccans  throughout history, up until the modern era.

The architecture of a riad is quite interesting. They are built for the purpose of protection and and introspection, it's as if when you enter a riad you are secluded from the outside world. The focus of all the rooms is directed towards a beautifully designed fountain in the middle of the courtyard. The building has usually no Windows that face the outside, you can access it only through a gate. However, all the Windows are opened to the open space in the middle towards the fountain. The riads are also built this way because Moroccans used to live throughout their lives as a family, even when the son marries, he doesn't leave home.

Nowadays the riads are open to visitors. Not many Moroccans live in riads anymore. Which leaves a lot of them to be turned into beautiful hotels, restaurants or cafes. Others are open for visitors to explore them.
Borj Fez

Staying in the old Medina of Fez for a long period of time may feel like time travel to past centuries. You might want to get a taste of the modern lifestyle, or perhaps even a taste of foods that you got used to in your country. Visiting Borj Fez can offer this to you. Borj Fez is big mall in Fez that you must visit. There you can do all sorts of shopping and fun activities. There you can find worldwide restaurants that offer foods like burgers, pizza and tacos.

Finally, you may have felt some excitement as you read along these lines, a desire to visit the city and experience a feeling that you might not have had before. There's always something new to do while in Fez city, other than the things mentioned in here. If you found this a pleasurable experience, please share your opinions with us and let other people know about your trip to Fez and the things you've done there, in the comments below.
However, if you want to visit Fez and need any help in making that easy please contact our services.

title: 3 best activities to do while traveling Morocco

description: Morocco has a lot of things to experience and to see, while traveling morocco you probably wonder what type of activities you can do, you may think of big

blocks.x: by webdono
| Uncategorized

Morocco has a lot of things to experience and to see, while traveling morocco you probably wonder what type of activities you can do, you may think of big cities like Marrakech, Fes or Casablanca at first, while these cities reflects both traditional and modern morocco, there is another hidden Morocco to be discovers through new activities, activities that not so many tourists think of, in this article I invite you to discover the Moroccan culture in a more deeper level, in a way that you will consider going not only to the big cities and famous places but to give a thought about going to villages, small towns and hidden places.
Here are 3 different activities to consider while travelling Morocco
The Ouzoud Waterfalls

The ouzoud falls are a series of falls located in the center of morocco in the high mountains of the Atlas region, near Beni Mellal and Azilal the town famous by its handmade rugs and other crafts, it is one of the places that are easily accessible for visitors and tourists as there is public transportation available and very affordable for everyone, but also there is a possibility to book a guided tours from Marrakech or from other cities like Azilal or Beni Mellal directly to ouzoud falls and that includes transportations, food and also drinks and some other services depending on what company you book with.

The Ouzoud water falls are a very peaceful place to enjoy the sounds of water flowing, the sounds of birds, the fresh air and the amazing sights. There is a presence of a bunch of restaurant and local food services that offers Tajines, Couscous, mint tea or other local dishes, you may also notice some monkeys while you are around, they are generally very approachable and don’t hurt people as they are familiar with their presence, but be careful as they can steal your food, so watch out!

Enjoy the spectacular view of these falls, cross the river to the other side to take picture and to get the most out of your visit, we recommend visiting Ouzoud during the week and not in the weekends as it gets busy sometimes so its hard to enjoy it to the fullest.
Desert Safari trip

One of the best activities you can do while traveling morocco, is going on a safari to the desert, at merzouga town particularly as it is the most famous spot for desert excursions lovers or any other southern Moroccan city, the things you can do on your trip to the Sahara are numerous and fun, for example  you can ride camels, camp, eat traditional tajines, enjoy sunset in the middle of the Sahara, or rent a quad to drive in the huge dunes
At your arrival, you will get your blue scarf to put it on you like the locals in order to protect you from the sun and the sand as the weather in this region in Morocco can be though sometimes
Wander and take pictures in the massive sand dunes, take desktop pictures also if you are into this because I assure you it is nothing like you’ve seen before

If you decided to spend the night there, remember to bring a warm jacket and some warm clothes as it gets cold at night, but eventually you can light up some fire in the camp in order to get warm and enjoy talking to people traveling with you around it along with mint tea or coffee and make some new connections and why not friendships.
Wake up to a beautiful sunrise from the dunes and the huge amount of sand, creating a palette of colors that will amaze you and make you want to take picture of such a beautiful scene.
Asilah Town

This time it’s a city in north Morocco, it is a unique city that will remind you of both Chefchaouen and Essaouira if it happened that you visited them both, a coastal peaceful city , not far from Tangier, it is a an underrated  town, characterized by its narrow streets, with a mixture of white blue and green painted murals, deserted in the winter season but full of tourists during the summer, that are mainly Moroccans, external tourists in Asilah are rare, at the exception of Spanish people that mostly come for a quick visit to the north of Morocco during the weekends if they can, it’s very small that you can finish the tour of the whole town in less than 3 hours

Local restaurants serve fish mainly, and at breakfast you can have fresh orange juice, mint tea or a cup of coffee and milk, along with Msemen, another local breakfast meal is paissar which is a soup from dry lentils served with olive oil during the winter months

A big percentage of the people in asilah speak Spanish along with Arabic instead of French and this is due to the history of Spanish colonization of the northern morocco back then in the early 1900, the Spanish touch is appearing in the architecture of some buildings around the city
Aqilah is a calm and comfortable city that you should definitely include in your to do list of traveling Morocco, at least for a quick visit.

These were 3 activities to do while traveling Morocco, of course there is a multitude of activities you can do in this north African country, it is really the country of contrasts as you can experience hot weather degrees on a region and just near it on another region you can be surprised by snow and snowy peaks and on another green lands and trees
So, what is your next activity in morocco, are you willing to visit morocco any soon?
